what: Bonsai 27B: A 27B-Class model that runs on a phone

clean_source_blocks.text: Article URL: https://prismml.com/news/bonsai-27b Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48910545 Points: 394 # Comments: 148

PrismML is back in the news today after the AI startup’s CEO told CNBC that Apple is looking at the company’s technology. The company has also released its Bonsai 27B model that it says runs on iPhone, iPad, and Mac. PrismML first made headlines last week when The Information reported on the AI startup. That report included mention of PrismML holding meetings with Apple about “ways it could use its technology.” The report also noted PrismML’s Bonsai 27B model, scheduled for release today. As expected, PrismML has now released that model: Bonsai 27B reaches up to 163 tok/s in 1-bit and 134 tok/s in Ternary on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090. On an M5 Max, it reaches up to 87 tok/s in 1-bit and 58 tok/s in Ternary.

Ternary Bonsai 27B uses ternary {−1, 0, +1} weights with FP16 group-wise scaling, giving a true 1.71 effective bits per weight. At 5.9 GB, it is the quality-oriented variant: it runs on an everyday laptop with the full reasoning, tool-calling, and agentic capability. 1-bit Bonsai 27B uses binary {−1, +1} weights with the same group-wise scaling, giving 1.125 effective bits per weight. At 3.9 GB, it is the footprint-oriented variant, which fits within the memory budget of an iPhone 17 Pro, bringing a 27B-class model onto a phone for the first time.

A 27B model in standard 16-bit precision needs about 54GB of memory. Even a well-built 4-bit quantization comes in around 18GB — too large for a phone, and too large for most laptops as well. That’s been the practical ceiling for local deployment: you could shrink an 8B model down to something a phone could hold, but a 27B model, with everything that extra scale buys in reasoning and instruction-following, stayed locked to the cloud or to machines with serious amounts of RAM. Bonsai 27B is PrismML’s answer to that ceiling, and it ships in two variants built for two different constraints.

Today, we're announcing Bonsai 27B, based on Qwen3.6 27B, the new multimodal flagship of the Bonsai family and the first model of its capability class to run on a phone.

Our earlier releases proved that models with 1-bit and ternary weights could produce commercially useful language models. Bonsai 27B extends that frontier to a new capability tier: multi-step reasoning, structured tool calls, vision tasks, and computer-use agentic loops that stay coherent across many steps. Until today, deploying that tier locally has been impractical for a concrete reason: a 27B model occupies roughly 54GB in 16-bit precision, and even a good 4-bit build, at 18GB, is too large for a phone and for most laptops.

Bonsai 27B changes that. It comes in two variants:

Ternary Bonsai 27B uses ternary {−1, 0, +1} weights with FP16 group-wise scaling, giving a true 1.71 effective bits per weight. At 5.9 GB, it is the quality-oriented variant: it runs on an everyday laptop with the full reasoning, tool-calling, and agentic capability.

As with every Bonsai release, the low-bit representation runs end to end across the language network, embeddings, attention, MLPs, and the LM head, with no higher-precision escape hatches. Both variants are multimodal, with the vision tower shipping in a compact 4-bit form so on-device workflows can see screenshots, documents, and camera input, not just text. Bonsai 27B carries a full 262K-token context, and supports speculative-decoding, compounding the speed with lossless draft-and-verify acceleration. Models aren’t only getting smarter — some companies are also working to make them smaller.

PrismML has released Bonsai 27B, the newest and largest member of its Bonsai family, and the first model in the 27-billion-parameter class built to run on a phone. The model is based on Qwen3.6 27B, and the release marks the point where PrismML’s compression work moves from small, novelty-sized models into genuinely capable, flagship-tier territory — the kind that can reason through multi-step problems, call tools, read screenshots, and hold up across long agentic loops.

This is PrismML’s third major release in the Bonsai line. The company first introduced 1-bit Bonsai 8B, packing an 8.2 billion parameter model into just over a gigabyte. It followed that with Ternary Bonsai, which used 1.58-bit weights to hit a 9x memory reduction while staying close to full-precision benchmark scores. Bonsai 27B pushes both approaches up to a scale that was previously assumed to be off-limits for on-device deployment entirely.

That’s been the practical ceiling for local deployment: you could shrink an 8B model down to something a phone could hold, but a 27B model, with everything that extra scale buys in reasoning and instruction-following, stayed locked to the cloud or to machines with serious amounts of RAM.

It comes in at 5.9GB, which is small enough to run comfortably on a regular laptop, and it’s positioned as the quality-first option — full reasoning, tool-calling, and agentic capability intact.

payload.title: PrismML julkaisi Bonsai 27B:n – 3,9 gigatavun versio mahtuu yhtiön mukaan iPhone 17 Prohon
payload.summary: PrismML kertoo pakkaustekniikkansa mahdollistavan 27 miljardin parametrin tekoälymallin paikallisen käytön puhelimessa, tabletissa ja tietokoneessa.
payload.content:
PrismML on julkaissut Bonsai 27B -tekoälymallin, jonka 3,9 gigatavun 1-bittisen version yhtiö kertoo mahtuvan iPhone 17 Pron muistibudjettiin. Julkaisu pyrkii tuomaan 27 miljardin parametrin kokoluokan mallin puhelimeen, kun tämän kokoiset mallit ovat tavallisesti vaatineet pilvipalvelua tai runsaasti muistia.

## Kaksi eri tavoin pakattua versiota

Tavanomaisella 16 bitin tarkkuudella 27 miljardin parametrin malli tarvitsee noin 54 gigatavua muistia. Myös neljään bittiin kvantisoitu versio vie noin 18 gigatavua. Bonsai 27B:n ratkaisu on pudottaa painojen esitystarkkuus selvästi tätä alemmas ja käyttää samalla ryhmäkohtaista FP16-skaalausta.

Pienempi 1-bittinen versio käyttää binäärisiä painoja, joiden arvot ovat −1 tai +1. Sen tehollinen tarkkuus on 1,125 bittiä painoa kohti. PrismML kuvaa 3,9 gigatavun pakettia tilankäyttöön optimoiduksi vaihtoehdoksi ja väittää sen tuovan 27B-kokoluokan mallin ensimmäistä kertaa puhelimeen.

Laatuun painottuva Ternary-versio käyttää puolestaan arvoja −1, 0 ja +1. Sen tehollinen tarkkuus on 1,71 bittiä painoa kohti ja koko 5,9 gigatavua. Yhtiön mukaan versio toimii tavallisessa kannettavassa ja säilyttää päättely-, työkalukutsu- ja agenttitoiminnot.

## Nopeusluvut vaihtelevat laitteittain

PrismML:n omissa suorituskykymittauksissa 1-bittinen malli saavuttaa Nvidia GeForce RTX 5090 -näytönohjaimella enimmillään 163 tokenia sekunnissa ja Ternary-versio 134 tokenia sekunnissa. M5 Max -järjestelmässä vastaavat huippuluvut ovat 87 ja 58 tokenia sekunnissa.

Yhtiön mukaan Bonsai 27B toimii iPhonen lisäksi iPadissa ja Macissa. PrismML on saanut huomiota myös Apple-yhteyksistään: The Information kertoi yhtiöiden tavanneen keskustellakseen tavoista, joilla Apple voisi hyödyntää teknologiaa. PrismML:n toimitusjohtaja on lisäksi sanonut CNBC:lle Applen tarkastelevan yhtiön teknologiaa.

Julkaistut koko- ja nopeusluvut ovat PrismML:n ilmoittamia. Puhelinkäytön todellinen suorituskyky, energiankulutus ja mallin laadun säilyminen eivät käy ilmi esitetyistä luvuista, joten väitteet tarvitsevat vielä riippumatonta käytännön testausta.

Yhtiön ilmoittamat suorituskykyluvut perustuvat RTX 5090- ja M5 Max -järjestelmillä tehtyihin mittauksiin.

Article URL: https://prismml.com/news/bonsai-27b Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=48910545 Points: 394 # Comments: 148

PrismML is back in the news today after the AI startup’s CEO told CNBC that Apple is looking at the company’s technology. The company has also released its Bonsai 27B model that it says runs on iPhone, iPad, and Mac. PrismML first made headlines last week when The Information reported on the AI startup. That report included mention of PrismML holding meetings with Apple about “ways it could use its technology.” The report also noted PrismML’s Bonsai 27B model, scheduled for release today. As expected, PrismML has now released that model: Bonsai 27B reaches up to 163 tok/s in 1-bit and 134 tok/s in Ternary on an NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090. On an M5 Max, it reaches up to 87 tok/s in 1-bit and 58 tok/s in Ternary.

Ternary Bonsai 27B uses ternary {−1, 0, +1} weights with FP16 group-wise scaling, giving a true 1.71 effective bits per weight. At 5.9 GB, it is the quality-oriented variant: it runs on an everyday laptop with the full reasoning, tool-calling, and agentic capability. 1-bit Bonsai 27B uses binary {−1, +1} weights with the same group-wise scaling, giving 1.125 effective bits per weight. At 3.9 GB, it is the footprint-oriented variant, which fits within the memory budget of an iPhone 17 Pro, bringing a 27B-class model onto a phone for the first time.

A 27B model in standard 16-bit precision needs about 54GB of memory. Even a well-built 4-bit quantization comes in around 18GB — too large for a phone, and too large for most laptops as well. That’s been the practical ceiling for local deployment: you could shrink an 8B model down to something a phone could hold, but a 27B model, with everything that extra scale buys in reasoning and instruction-following, stayed locked to the cloud or to machines with serious amounts of RAM. Bonsai 27B is PrismML’s answer to that ceiling, and it ships in two variants built for two different constraints.
